# Jubilees Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Prologue — Revelation to Moses on Sinai

---

**1:1** It came to pass in the first year of the exodus of the children of Israel from Egypt, in the third month, on the sixteenth day of the month, that God spoke to Moses, saying: "Come up to me on the mountain, and I will give you two stone tablets of the law and the commandment which I have written, so that you may teach them."

**1:2** Moses went up to the mountain of God. The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai, and a cloud overshadowed it for six days.

**1:3** On the seventh day he called to Moses from within the cloud, and the appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a burning fire on the summit of the mountain.

**1:4** Moses remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights, and God taught him the earlier and the later history — all the divisions of the days of the law and the testimony.

**1:5** He said: "Pay careful attention to all the words I speak to you today. Write them in a book, so that future generations may see that I have not abandoned them, despite all the evil they have done in transgressing the covenant I am establishing between me and you this day on Mount Sinai."

**1:6** "When all these things come upon them, they will acknowledge that I am more righteous than they in all my judgments and in all my dealings, and they will know that I have truly been with them."

**1:7** "Now write down for yourself all these words I am declaring to you today, for I know their rebellion and their stubbornness — even before I bring them into the land I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob: 'To your descendants I will give a land flowing with milk and honey.'"

**1:8** "They will eat and be satisfied, then turn to foreign gods — gods who cannot deliver them from any of their troubles — and this testimony will stand as a witness against them."

**1:9** "For they will forget all my commandments — everything I command them — and follow the nations and their impurity and their shameful practices. They will serve their gods, and those gods will become a snare, an affliction, a torment, and a trap for them."

**1:10** "Many will perish; they will be seized and fall into enemy hands, because they forsook my statutes, my commandments, my covenant festivals, my sabbaths, my holy things which I sanctified among them, my tabernacle and my sanctuary which I made holy in their midst, and my name that dwells upon them."

**1:11** "They will build high places, set up sacred pillars, and carve idols for themselves, bowing down to the work of their own hands — each to his own image — and these things will become a stumbling block to them."

**1:12** "I will send witnesses among them to testify against them, but they will not listen; they will kill those witnesses also, and persecute those who seek the law, abolishing and changing everything in order to do evil before my eyes."

**1:13** "I will hide my face from them and deliver them into the hands of the nations — to captivity, to plunder, and to destruction. I will drive them out of the land and scatter them among all the nations."

**1:14** "They will forget all my law, all my commandments, and all my ordinances, and they will go astray concerning the new moons, the sabbaths, the festivals, the jubilees, and the appointed times."

**1:15** "But after this they will return to me from among the nations with all their heart, all their soul, and all their strength. I will gather them from among all the nations, and they will seek me — and I will be found by them when they seek me with their whole heart and their whole soul."

**1:16** "I will reveal to them abundant peace, and I will establish them as a planting of righteousness with all my heart and all my soul. They shall be a blessing and not a curse; they shall be the head and not the tail."

**1:17** "I will build my sanctuary in their midst. I will dwell with them, I will be their God, and they shall be my true and righteous people."

**1:18** "I will not abandon them, nor will I be estranged from them, for I am the LORD their God."

**1:19** Then Moses fell on his face and prayed: "O LORD my God, do not abandon your people and your inheritance so that they wander in the error of their hearts. Do not hand them over to their enemies the nations, lest those nations rule over them and lead them into sin against you."

**1:20** "Let your mercy be lifted over your people, O LORD. Create in them an upright spirit, and do not let the spirit of Beliar rule over them to accuse them before you and lead them away from every righteous path, causing them to perish from before your face."

**1:21** "They are your people and your inheritance — those whom you delivered with your great power from the hand of the Egyptians. Create in them a clean heart and a holy spirit, and do not let them be ensnared in their sins from this time forward and forever."

**1:22** The LORD said to Moses: "I know their perversity and their thoughts and their stubbornness. They will not be obedient until they confess their own sin and the sins of their ancestors."

**1:23** "But after this they will return to me completely — with all their heart and all their soul. I will circumcise the foreskin of their heart and of their descendants' hearts, and I will create a holy spirit within them. I will purify them so that they will never again turn away from me — from that day forward and forever."

**1:24** "Their souls will cling to me and to all my commandments. They will carry out my commandments, and I will be their Father and they shall be my children."

**1:25** "All of them will be called children of the living God. Every angel and every spirit will know — they shall all know — that these are my children, and that I am their Father in sincerity and righteousness, and that I love them."

**1:26** "Write for Moses all the words I am telling you: the things of the beginning and the things of the end — everything that will come to pass through all the divisions of the days of the law and the testimony, through the weeks and the jubilees — until I descend and dwell with them for all eternity."

**1:27** He said to the angel of the presence: "Write for Moses from the beginning of creation until the time my sanctuary is built among them forever."

**1:28** "The LORD will appear before the eyes of all, and everyone will know that I am the God of Israel, the Father of all the children of Jacob, and King on Mount Zion forever. Zion and Jerusalem shall be holy."

**1:29** The angel of the presence, who went before the camp of Israel, took the tablets recording the divisions of the years — from the time of creation, through the law and the testimony, through the weeks of jubilees, year by year — and he narrated to Moses all the divisions of the days of the law and the testimony, until he had finished.

---
*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows LOGOS formal register throughout. Key theological terms retained: "Beliar" (v.20), "angel of the presence" (vv.27-29), "planting of righteousness" (v.16). See disagreement log for divergences on vv.1, 16, 20.*
